claims.statement: For every ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star with m>=100, N=sum_i r_i, h=1+2a2+4a3+7a4, C=G product_i B_(r_i), E=zL^N, and U_i=G B_(r_i-1) product_(ell!=i) B_(r_ell), every represented tip branch i and every integer 1<=k with 2k<=N+2 satisfy (h+1)U_i[k]C[k]+(k+1)(h-k+1)(E[k]C[k]-E[k+1]C[k-1])>0, with integer zero-extended coefficients.
claims.scope: Census-free informal tail theorem for m>=100 on the registered ordinary path-star family, for every represented tip and the full guarded band 1<=k<=floor((N+2)/2); no first-descent, eligibility, or selector premise. This does not cover m<100, the endpoint shifted comparison without its separate LR bridge, an arbitrary tree, or a formal award.
claims.reason: The report gives a full two-band proof, including exact low-rank support handling, the binomial-log-concavity repair for the second curvature bracket, direct full-Jensen specialization to the factors of U_i, even/odd midpoint bounds, exact Taylor constants, and positive denominator clearing. The retained exact arithmetic is targeted bounded corroboration only.

limitations: The complete m<100 surplus base remains unproved here.
This surplus composition has no C6 governed Lean award.
The endpoint shifted comparison still requires the separate main-product LR bridge; coefficientwise endpoint dominance alone is insufficient.
The result is a stronger sufficient tip condition and does not change the distinct selected payment or MASS grades, the family aggregate scope, or any arbitrary-tree Erdős993 claim.
